dialogue.content: こんにちは。よろしくお願いいたします。
dialogue.English: Hello. It's nice to meet you.

dialogue.content: よろしくお願いします！
dialogue.English: It's nice to meet you too!

dialogue.content: 相談員です。こちらこそよろしくお願いいたします。今日はどうされましたか？
dialogue.English: I'm your counselor. It's a pleasure to meet you as well. What brings you here today?

dialogue.content: 以前から、母親との関係に悩んでいて、どうにかしたいと思って相談させてもらいました
dialogue.English: I've been struggling with my relationship with my mother for a while, and I wanted to do something about it, so I decided to seek counseling.

dialogue.content: お母さまとのご関係でお悩みなんですね。具体的にどういう場面で悩んでおられるとか教えていただけますか？
dialogue.English: So you're having difficulty in your relationship with your mother. Could you tell me more about the kinds of situations that feel challenging?

dialogue.content: もともと性格があまり合わず、実家に帰ると、最初は良いんですが、少しずつイライラが募ってしまいます
dialogue.English: We've never really had compatible personalities, and when I go back home, it's fine at first, but I gradually get more and more irritated.

dialogue.content: きつい言い方ではないけど、自分の意見を押し付けられるというか…
dialogue.English: It's not said in a harsh way, but it feels like her opinions are being imposed on me...

dialogue.content: お母さまとの性格や考え方の違いを感じておられて、違う考え方を押し付けられているように感じられているのですね。
dialogue.English: You sense differences in personality and perspective with your mother, and it feels as though her way of thinking is being imposed on you.

dialogue.content: そうなんです！
dialogue.English: Exactly!

dialogue.content: なるほど、たまにかえってお顔を見た時にいろいろ言われるのは疲れるとお感じなんですね。
dialogue.English: I see, so you feel it's tiring when you go home to see her and she tells you all sorts of things.

dialogue.content: そうですね！根本的な考え方が違うというのもあるんですが…私が言ったことや、相談したことに対して、すぐ結論をつけたがるというか…「それは仕方ないじゃん」「そんなに言うなら〇〇すれば」と、すぐに自分の判断を伝えてきます
dialogue.English: That's right! Part of it is that our fundamental ways of thinking are different... but also, whenever I say something or ask for advice, she tends to jump to conclusions. She'll immediately give me her judgment, saying things like, 'That can't be helped,' or 'If you're going to complain so much, you should just do XX.'

dialogue.content: 指示的なんですかね？
dialogue.English: I guess you could call it being directive?

dialogue.content: 相談者さんのご相談に寄り添うというより、アドバイスを出してこられる傾向が強くて、その方向性がご自身の考え方と違うといったところでしょうか？
dialogue.English: So, rather than empathizing with what you're trying to discuss, she has a strong tendency to give advice, and the direction of that advice differs from your own way of thinking, is that right?

dialogue.content: そうかもです！確かに、寄り添ってもらってる感じは全然ないです
dialogue.English: That might be it! It's true, I don't feel like she's empathizing with me at all.

dialogue.content: 方向性と言われると、母親が言ってきたアドバイスの内容を覚えてないかもしれません笑
dialogue.English: When you mention 'direction,' I realize I might not even remember the content of the advice my mother has given me (laughs).

dialogue.content: ご相談者さんにご兄弟とかおられますか？
dialogue.English: Do you have any siblings?

dialogue.content: 兄が1人います
dialogue.English: I have one older brother.

dialogue.content: なるほど、方向性を誘導されているように感じられると、折角よいアドバイスをされても入って来ないんですね？
dialogue.English: I see. When you feel you're being steered in a certain direction, even good advice doesn't really sink in, does it?

dialogue.content: お兄様がおられるのですね。お兄様とはそのようなお話はされますか？
dialogue.English: So you have an older brother. Do you ever talk with him about these kinds of things?

dialogue.content: うーん、どうなんでしょう？最近は、もう「また自分の意見しか言わないじゃん」と感じて、ハイハイって感じで聞いてしまっているかもです
dialogue.English: Hmm, I'm not sure. Lately, I find myself thinking, 'There she goes again, only saying her own opinion,' and I just end up nodding along.

dialogue.content: 兄とは、そこまで仲良くなくてそんな話は全然したことないですどちらかというと、兄と母はお互いに依存してる気がするし…
dialogue.English: I'm not that close with my brother, so we've never talked about things like this. If anything, I feel like my brother and mother are dependent on each other...

dialogue.content: だんだんとお母さまのそういう傾向を受け入れかけているというか、もう仕方ないのではないかと思い始めておられるのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Are you starting to feel that this is just how your mother is, and that there's not much you can do about it?

dialogue.content: あ、そうですね
dialogue.English: Ah, yes, that's right.

dialogue.content: もう仕方ないって思っちゃってますね
dialogue.English: I've started to think it just can't be helped.

dialogue.content: けど結局、２日３日と一緒にいるとイライラしてきちゃった、態度に出てしまいます
dialogue.English: But in the end, if I'm with her for two or three days, I get irritated and it shows in my attitude.

dialogue.content: 母も、もう高齢なので、優しくしなきゃって思ってるんですが…自宅に帰ってきてから、いつも後悔しています…
dialogue.English: My mother is getting older, so I know I should be kinder to her... but I always regret it after I get back home.

dialogue.content: お兄様とお母さまのご関係とはまた違う感じなんですね。お兄様にそのような悩みをご相談されても、ご理解していただけなさそうですか？
dialogue.English: It sounds like your relationship with your mother is different from your brother's. Do you feel that even if you shared this concern with him, he might not really understand?

dialogue.content: 長時間ご実家におれられると、態度に出てしまい、ご自身も後悔されてお辛く感じられるのでしょうか。
dialogue.English: When you spend a long time at your parents' home, it starts to show in your attitude, and you end up regretting it and feeling distressed—is that right?

dialogue.content: なんて言われるのか、想像すらつきません笑母親以上に、私と兄との関係性が薄くて、小さな悩みだったとしても、相談する発想にならないのが本音です…
dialogue.English: I can't even imagine what he would say, haha. Honestly, my relationship with my brother is even more distant than the one with my mother, so the thought of confiding in him, even about a small problem, just doesn't occur to me.

dialogue.content: そうですねあと何年、母親が元気でいられるか分からないので、今のうちに優しくしなきゃと思って…
dialogue.English: Right. I don't know how many more years my mother will be well, so I feel I should be kind to her while I still can.

dialogue.content: なるほど、お兄様にご相談するのも少し難しそうですね・・
dialogue.English: I see. So it also feels a bit difficult to talk with your brother about this...

dialogue.content: それに大人になってから、母親なりに頑張ってたんだなって思えるようにもなったので、余計に労ってあげたいなって気持ちも出てきました
dialogue.English: And as I've grown older, I've come to realize that, in her own way, my mother was doing her best, so I feel even more that I want to care for her.

dialogue.content: ご年齢的にもお母さまの事をご心配されておられるのですね。そういうお優しいお気持ちはお母さまにしっかり伝わっていると思います。
dialogue.English: You're also concerned about your mother because of her age. I believe that your kind feelings are surely getting through to her.

dialogue.content: だと良いんですけど…
dialogue.English: I hope so, but...

dialogue.content: お母さん的には「楽しかった」って言ってるので、私がイライラしてるのは気づいてないのか、意に介してないような感じはあります笑
dialogue.English: From her perspective, she always says she 'had a good time,' so I feel like she either doesn't notice I'm irritated or just doesn't care, haha.

dialogue.content: お母さま的にはお話されててすっきりされているのかもしれませんね。
dialogue.English: Perhaps for your mother, talking with you is a way for her to feel refreshed.

dialogue.content: 確かに、お母さんはスッキリしてそうです笑父と兄といるのに息が詰まるみたいで、それで遊びに来たりもします
dialogue.English: That's true, she does seem refreshed, haha. It seems she feels stifled being with my father and brother, and that's one of the reasons she comes to visit.

dialogue.content: 私は最後の方はイライラしてるんですけど、「楽しかった」と言って帰っていきます…笑
dialogue.English: By the end I'm irritated, but she goes home saying, 'That was fun'... haha.

dialogue.content: お母さまは相談者さんと会えるのを待っておられて、会えた瞬間に一気にいろいろ言ってしまわれる感じでしょうか
dialogue.English: Perhaps your mother looks forward to seeing you, and the moment she does, everything she wants to say just comes pouring out at once.

dialogue.content: ご相談させていただき、ありがとうございました😊
dialogue.English: Thank you very much for this session. 😊

dialogue.content: こちらこそありがとうございました。今日ご相談していただいてどうでしたか？
dialogue.English: Thank you as well. How do you feel after our talk today?

dialogue.content: 話せて良かったです！またよろしくお願いします🤲
dialogue.English: I'm glad I was able to talk about it! I look forward to speaking with you again. 🤲

dialogue.content: またご相談にお越しください。ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Please feel free to come back for another consultation. Thank you.
